Quantum-vulnerable algorithms(2 groups · 3)
Public-key assets broken by a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer. Near-identical assets (same algorithm, finding and fix) share one card; open it for the list.
  • NIST Level 0: no quantum resistance. A large quantum computer running Shor's algorithm breaks it, whatever the key size (RSA, elliptic curves, Diffie-Hellman). Next: Level 1 needs a NIST post-quantum algorithm (FIPS 203 key exchange, FIPS 204 or 205 signature) at least as hard to break as AES-128; a hybrid key exchange counts as ready.
